 SC shields homebuyers from bank recovery without probe into builder-bank nexus
 SECTIONS SC shields homebuyers from bank recovery without probe into builder-bank nexus ET Online Last Updated: Nov 20, 2026, 03:34:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis The Supreme Court has provided relief to homebuyers by preventing loans from being repaid without proper investigation. Buyers in Gurugram faced recovery action despite not receiving their flats, leading to the court's intervention. The court stated that commercial courts must assess the potential collusion between bank officials and builders prior to taking action. Allegations of misuse of housing loan schemes have prompted further scrutiny in similar cases.
 Supreme Court has provided relief to homebuyers by preventing loans from being repaid without proper investigation
 The Supreme Court has directed commercial courts and insolvency tribunals not to order homebuyers to repay housing loans or take coercive recovery action without first examining whether banks disbursed funds to builders in violation of tripartite agreements, TOI reported on Friday.
 The ruling offers relief to buyers whose housing projects remain incomplete despite banks releasing a substantial portion of the sanctioned loans to developers.
The court said the liability of homebuyers must be assessed before they are directed to pay instalments, particularly in cases where a possible nexus between builders and bank officials needs to be examined, the report added. 
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order on a petition filed by buyers in Raheja Developers' Krishna housing project in Gurugram, which is undergoing insolvency proceedings . The buyers had approached the court after a bank initiated recovery proceedings against them in a commercial court in Saket, New Delhi, despite their not having received possession of their flats, according to the TOI report.
The bench said it was the duty of the commercial court to determine whether bank officials and the builder had colluded and whether loan disbursals were made in accordance with the tripartite agreement. Under such agreements, banks are required to release funds directly to developers in proportion to construction progress.
 Live Events
 The Supreme Court directed the civil court not to take coercive action against the petitioners or similarly placed buyers unless it first established that they had defaulted on their repayment obligations.
 The order comes amid wider concerns over alleged collusion between banks and developers under housing loan subvention schemes. In September last year, a Supreme Court bench led by Justice Kant ordered a CBI investigation into allegations that builders and banks had misused such schemes, leaving homebuyers burdened with loan repayments for unfinished projects.
The bench also noted that a growing number of distressed buyers were approaching the Supreme Court directly and said it might not be able to entertain fresh cases. In a separate Bengaluru project involving more than 4,000 buyers, it granted protection against possible bank recovery action and asked them to seek further relief from the Karnataka High Court .
